classification.difficultyReason: Interpret solutions as horizontal-line intersections, partition the output values at three turning-point heights, and distinguish tangency cases from the open intervals between them.

content.prompt: The diagram below shows the graph of a function $y=f(x)$. Find the value(s) of $k$ such that $f(x)=k$ has

spec.description: Schematic continuous curve reconstructed with smooth Bézier segments because no function rule is supplied. Preserve both rising ends, the three labelled turning points, the origin crossing, the left-branch crossing and the absence of numerical ticks.
spec.mathematics: Turning points (-1,-19), (1,13), (2,8), in increasing x order. The global minimum is -19; the other critical heights are 8 and 13.
spec.answerVisibility: All supplied points and labels remain visible in the question; no horizontal solution lines are added.

answer.worked: The horizontal line $y=-19$ touches the graph at its lowest point and has no other intersection. Hence $k=-19$.
For $-19<k<8$, the horizontal line $y=k$ crosses the two branches around the lowest turning point. For $k>13$, it crosses the two outer branches. Thus $-19<k<8$ or $k>13$.
At either $y=8$ or $y=13$, the horizontal line touches one turning point and crosses the curve at two other points. Hence $k=8$ or $k=13$.
Between the turning-point heights 8 and 13, a horizontal line crosses all four branches. Hence $8<k<13$.
